did_you_know.text: Did you know? Josiah celebrated Passover in Jerusalem, and the Passover sacrifice was offered on the fourteenth day of Nisan, the first month.

Did you know? Josiah instructed the Levites to return the Ark of the Covenant to the Temple that Solomon had built, so that they would no longer carry it on their shoulders but could devote themselves to serving the LORD and his people.
Did you know? Josiah donated 30,000 sheep and goats for the Passover, as well as 3,000 cattle, from his personal property.

Did you know? The officials of the priests also contributed animals for the Passover: 2,600 sheep and goats and 300 cattle. The officials of the Levites contributed 5,000 sheep and goats and 500 cattle.
Did you know? The Passover service was divided among them: the priests sprinkled the blood, while the Levites skinned the sacrifices and prepared them for distribution and offering.
Did you know? The Levites also prepared the Passover offerings for the priests, because the priests were busy offering the burnt offerings and the fat until nightfall.
Did you know? The singers and gatekeepers remained at their posts throughout the Passover service and were not required to leave their duties, because the other Levites prepared what they needed.
Did you know? At that time, the Israelites celebrated Passover and the Feast of Unleavened Bread for seven days.
Did you know? The Book of Chronicles describes this Passover as one that had not been celebrated like it since the days of the prophet Samuel. It was held in the eighteenth year of Josiah’s reign.

Did you know? After the Passover festival, Josiah went out to meet Neco, king of Egypt, who was marching to fight at Carchemish on the Euphrates, even though Neco said that his war was not directed against Judah.
Did you know? After Josiah died, Jeremiah composed a lament for him, and the male and female singers sang laments about him that became an established tradition in Israel.
